children: New Delhi, Oct. 19 -- Indian public sector enterprise Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) is all set to announce its financial results for the quarter ending on 30 September, 2026, on Monday, 19 October.

IREDA share price ended Friday's session on a positive note, closed 0.50% higher at Rs.108.80 per share on NSE. The PSU stock has remained weak in the near-term by falling over 2% in a month and 16.40% in six months. Furthermore, the stock continued to give negative returns by descending 22% on year-to-date (YTD) basis and 28% in a year.
Looking at the broader level, IREDA shares have delivered over 73.39% returns since its listing in November 2023.

According to Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, the fundamental narrative remains anchored by robust loan sanctions and sustained double-digit disbursement growth exceeding Rs.90,000 crore, solidifying its dominant position in financing India's non-fossil energy transition.

Srivastava further explained that market sentiment hinges heavily on asset quality metrics, specifically whether gross and net non-performing asset levels moderate or require elevated provisioning for stressed renewable developer exposures.
Additionally, net interest margins face scrutiny as borrowing costs versus lending yields dictate bottom-line expansion in a shifting rate environment.
Srivastava said that investors buying ahead of the print introduces binary event risk, as pre-results positions are acutely vulnerable to short-term volatility or post-announcement profit-taking.

"Instead of committing lump-sum capital before the numbers are public, a more measured strategy involves either phased systematic accumulation near key support zones or waiting for post-result clarity," she added.

She further added that confirming fresh slippage numbers, margin stability, and management guidance on full-year loan growth ensures long-term exposure to the green transition without bearing sudden downside surprises.
Meanwhile, Anuj Gupta, SEBI Registered Research Analyst, believes that investors can consider accumulating IREDA shares at current levels, as the stock is trading in the oversold zone.

"The stock recovered 4.21% last week to close at Rs.108.80, indicating improving momentum. From a technical perspective, the stock is showing positive signs of recovery, while its current valuation appears attractive from a fundamental standpoint. Investors with a long-term horizon may consider accumulating the stock in a staggered manner," Gupta said.

IREDA posted a 36.8% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs.337.5 crore in the first quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.246.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, supported by growth in its lending business.
The company's net interest income (NII), which reflects the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 24.1% to Rs.856.8 crore from Rs.690.5 crore a year earlier.
IREDA's outstanding loan book expanded to Rs.94,936 crore as of June 30, 2026, compared with Rs.79,941 crore on the same date last year.
